page: Google Cloud Platform m4n-ultramem-56 is a memory-optimized instance configuration designed for memory-intensive enterprise computing. It provides 56 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 architecture paired with 1488.0 GB of system memory. This yields an extensive memory-to-core allocation of approximately 26.57 GB of RAM per vCPU, placing it among the highest memory densities available in its compute class. The instance includes no integrated GPU accelerators.

Integrated local storage is absent on the m4n-ultramem-56, requiring all persistence layers and root volumes to operate over network-attached storage disks. As an instance in the network-optimized class, the architecture is tailored to handle high network traffic necessary for sustaining communication between remote block storage, clustered database nodes, and external data pipelines.

Cost efficiency on this platform is dictated by memory utilization. Given the heavy concentration of RAM relative to processor count, resource efficiency is highest when hosting memory-bound applications that require entire working sets in volatile memory. Workloads primarily constrained by CPU compute cycles or those requiring low-latency local NVMe drives represent an inefficient match for this hardware profile.

The m4n-ultramem-56 is suited for large-scale enterprise in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, extensive Redis or Memcached clusters, big data analytics engines, and large relational database management systems operating on substantial datasets.

This hardware architecture is specifically suited for massive in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, large-scale distributed caching layers, intensive real-time analytics engines, and high-capacity database systems that need substantial data retained in RAM without requiring local NVMe storage.
